summary: jenscolt's three dome cups (large eye, small eye, front sensor) as one revolved parametric cup with three parameter sets, each in its reference frame; nothing moves.

parts.name: eye
parts.role: the large eye dome (spideybot_eye.stl): a hollow cup, apex at low Y, open at high Y
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh, far from the others; N1 form part, not printed

parts.name: small-eye
parts.role: the small eye dome (spideybot_small_eye.stl), same cup with its own numbers
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh, far from the others; N1 form part, not printed

parts.name: sensor
parts.role: the front sensor dome (spideybot_sensor.stl), same cup with its own numbers
parts.why_separate: a separate jenscolt mesh, far from the others; N1 form part, not printed

options: revolved profile: flat apex, elliptic dome, straight wall
sphere cap minus an inner sphere
alternatives.choice: revolved profile: flat apex, elliptic dome, straight wall
alternatives.why: the meshes have a flat apex and a straight wall that a sphere cap cannot give; 5 numbers per cup

acceptance.text: each part is within p95 1.0 mm and max 2.5 mm of its reference, both ways
the small eye is within the same fidelity
the sensor is within the same fidelity
every sweep variant is one valid closed solid
one parametric cup (radius, depth, wall, rim) used by all three parts, each with its own numbers
not: build.py reads a mesh: the reference meshes are read only by the gates and the designer's probes
the default fidelity gate passes for each part, the sweep's variants are valid solids, and the judge scores ≥ 0.70 against the meshes
